A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same G-ZAP research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary sections are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated appendix content.

before.justification: v1 reports original pansharpening experiments on GF2, WV3, and WV2, including benchmark results, loss and backbone ablations, runtime measurements, and supplementary simulated-data results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds quantitative arbitrary-scale evaluation and comparisons with additional methods in supplementary Tables 5 and 6.

M1.justification: The INRConv architecture, three-level training procedure, losses, arbitrary-scale querying, and weight-reuse procedure remain unchanged. Equations 1–10 and the architecture diagrams retain the same content.

E1.justification: The datasets and pansharpening task remain unchanged. Supplementary Table 5 extends tested magnifications to ×2.1 and ×6.7, alongside ×3.4; ×6.7 adds a larger-scale extrapolation scenario beyond v1's displayed range up to ×4.

E2.justification: Supplementary Table 6 newly evaluates ADWM, Pan-Crafter, and INF3 on WV3 and GF2, substantially strengthening comparison with recent competitors and adding an explicit feature-based INR comparator. Table 5 also compares direct querying against Bic. and G-ZAP×1+Bic.; v1 already included qualitative interpolation comparisons.

E3.justification: Supplementary S2 adds a reference-based, reduced-resolution WV3 protocol comparing direct querying and interpolation at three scales using Q2n, SAM, ERGAS, and SCC. These metrics already appeared in Table 4. Existing training budgets and evaluation settings are retained; S3 states that its additional baselines use the same full-resolution protocol.

E4.justification: S2/Table 5 adds a quantitative check of whether arbitrary-scale querying improves on resizing the standard output, extending v1's qualitative analysis. Existing loss ablations, backbone comparisons, weight-reuse analyses, and convergence evidence are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional tables continue the existing practice of reporting point estimates without uncertainty.

E6.justification: Tables 5 and 6 add substantial numerical evidence for arbitrary-scale reconstruction and additional competitors. For example, Table 5 reports ×6.7 Q2n of 0.4926 for G-ZAP versus 0.4107 for G-ZAP×1+Bic. Table 1 also changes C-BDSD's GF2 Dλ from 0.0119 to 0.0619. Table 6's G-ZAP scores are rounded versions of existing results, not improved performance across versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and derivations in Section 3, including Equations 1–10, are unchanged. Neither version adds formal propositions or proofs; the new appendix interpretations are empirical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal claims: arbitrary-scale zero-shot fusion, three-level training, cross-scene and cross-sensor generalization, efficient weight reuse, and competitive performance without spatial-fidelity losses.

C2.justification: New S2 interprets the quantitative interpolation comparison as evidence of scale-aware reconstruction beyond merely resizing the ×1 output. New S3 interprets the INF3 comparison as supporting the importance of the zero-shot training framework for adapting feature-based INR representations.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 clarifies that external training sets serve pretrained baselines, while G-ZAP trains only on test image pairs. S4 newly states that supplementary videos are provided, although they are not embedded in the supplied PDFs. Optimizer, learning rate, epochs, loss weights, hardware, and the dataset access reference remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds six distinct references, covering MTF foundations, ADWM, Pan-Crafter, and two recent fusion papers. INF3 was already cited but becomes an evaluated comparator. The broader research positioning and novelty claims remain unchanged; consolidated duplicate references do not represent removed works.

P1.justification: Localized edits correct FMG-Pan to G-ZAP and INFFF to INF3, improve spacing and data-use wording, and add acknowledgements. The appendix gains two subsections and moves the convergence discussion after the visual comparisons, without extensive rewriting of the main narrative.

P2.justification: Two appendix tables are added, several existing figures are enlarged, and Tables 2 and 3 are relocated. The supplementary visual examples and convergence plot are reordered and renumbered. All ten existing figures retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens v1's visual arbitrary-scale evidence with quantitative interpolation controls in Table 5 and broadens competitive validation through Table 6, especially the INF3 comparison. Data-use clarification also improves readability. These are useful but bounded gains: construction of references at non-integer scales and setup of the added baselines remain briefly documented, limiting how thoroughly the new comparisons can be assessed.
